frame_21.jpg.note: Tiny blocky figures in identical poses stand evenly spaced on a flat plain, like game pieces on a board. The red-coat block is a rigid grid of clones. The cannonball stacks and crates look like props on a tabletop, and the figures have no real contact shadows.

frame_47.jpg.note: Almost the same as frame_21. The figures are stiff, upright, identical peg-like soldiers, spaced like chess pieces and staring straight ahead. They look pasted onto the flat pavement, with no weight or variation.

frame_58.jpg.note: Close up, the figures are low-poly blocky dolls with box torsos and stick legs. Every marching figure shares the same stride, and the women's skirts are plain cones. The light and long shadows help a little, but the figures are cloned in rows, with hard-edged hands and hats and flat white faces.

frame_40.jpg.note: Same blocky doll build as frame_58, with a small gain in realism from the cast sunlight. The marchers repeat one rigid scissor-step pose and the standing figures are stiff. Skirts are cone shapes and heads are simple boxes, so it reads as a diorama of figurines.
